subject: Request: Supplemental credit for public-interest annotation pilot
messages:
From: Dr. Laila Ahmad <laila.ahmad@openheritage.org>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, samir.patel@communitylabs.org
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Request: supplemental compute credit for annotation pilot

Hi Jonas,

Thank you again for the quick onboarding last month — the team at Open Heritage has been running human labeler passes against a 120k-image public-archive dataset, and we unexpectedly tripled our token usage after adding multi-turn context checks. Our grant covers research staff but not cloud costs, and we’ve hit the limit on our trial credits.

We’re asking whether Redwood can provide a one-time supplemental credit or trial extension (~30k–50k tokens or equivalent compute) so we can finish the annotation pass and produce the derived metadata for the museum partners. The work is non-commercial, and we’d be happy to provide a short write-up and attribution for Redwood in our public report.

Quick details:
- Pilot: archival-image annotation for descriptive metadata (object type, era, key persons)
- Current model: redwood/gpt-3.5-instruct (default)
- Expected remaining runtime: 10k–20k API calls over 2–3 weeks
- Fund status: grant closes Oct 15; no additional compute funds available until Nov

Attachments: annotation_guidelines_v2.pdf (sample prompt + QC).

Would be grateful for any promo credit or an extension on the trial window so we can finish the deliverable to our partners. Happy to sign an MOU if needed.

Best,
Laila
Dr. Laila Ahmad
Research Director, Open Heritage Collective


From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Laila Ahmad <laila.ahmad@openheritage.org>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: supplemental compute credit for annotation pilot

Hi Laila — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the guidelines. Really appreciate the public-report offer; that helps a lot.

A few quick questions so I can route this internally:
- Can you confirm the current monthly spend and the trial credit remaining (screenshot or a usage CSV is fine)?
- Are you tied to redwood/gpt-3.5-instruct for quality reasons, or would a quantized variant be acceptable?
- Timeline: you mentioned Oct 15 — is finishing the annotation pass before Oct 15 a hard deadline?

I’ve looped Ben on promo/credits — he’ll advise on what we can provision quickly. If it helps, please attach a very short statement we can reference in an MOU (non-legal summary of purpose, public deliverables, and attribution).

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: ben.carter@redwood.com <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Laila Ahmad <laila.ahmad@openheritage.org>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 25 Sep 2026 17:45:00 +0000
Subject: Promo support for Open Heritage annotation pilot

Hi Laila — Ben here (Redwood sales).

Thanks for the context — we can absolutely support non-commercial public-interest work like this. To move quickly I can provision a provisional promotional stipend: 35,000 token-equivalent credit applied to your account and a 30-day trial extension.

Conditions/outlines:
- Credit applied immediately on account upon receipt of a short (one-paragraph) project statement we can attach to our internal MAP (project purpose + deliverable + attribution text).
- We’ll set an upper daily usage cap so the credit lasts the window; if you expect spikes let us know so we can set a higher cadence.
- If the project will use a large-context model or non-standard quantized variant we’ll validate compatibility first (we can recommend a similar lower-cost variant).
- We’ll ask for a one-sheet public blurb after project completion (short quote/attribution).

Next steps:
1) Laila: send the one-paragraph project statement + current usage CSV (usage_report_q3.csv or a screenshot).
2) Marissa (CC’d, CS) will add the credit and configure caps.
3) If an MOU is required, I can route a simple DocuSign template (link below).

DocuSign/MOU (sample): https://docusign.redwood.com/templates/MOU-public-projects-2026
Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-annotation-guidelines

Happy to increase the stipend if the scope is larger, but this should cover the remaining annotation pass based on your estimate.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Laila Ahmad <laila.ahmad@openheritage.org>, samir.patel@communitylabs.org
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Supplemental credit for public-interest annotation pilot — approved

Hi Laila and Samir — quick note to confirm: Redwood will apply a 35,000-token promotional credit to the Open Heritage account and grant a 30-day trial extension effective today. Marissa will post the credit and set a daily cap (we set that conservatively at first; if you need higher throughput tell us).

Action items:
- Laila: please reply with the one-paragraph project statement and the usage CSV (attachment recommended).
- Marissa: please apply the credit and confirm the cap settings.
- Ben: please add the Docusign link if an MOU is requested by the finance team.

Check-in: let’s do a 20-minute sync one week from today to validate throughput and quality (Jonas + Ben + Marissa + Laila). I’ll send the calendar invite once Marissa confirms availability.

Thanks — glad we could make this work for a public-interest project.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Strategic Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
